interest: This document illustrates pre-World War II Japanese agricultural and industrial procurement efforts, specifically the attempt to acquire 40,000 flax plants from New Zealand in 1934 to develop or expand domestic fiber production. Although the underlying consular despatch is cross-referenced elsewhere in the State Department decimal filing system (847h.00/25), this record demonstrates how American consular posts across the Pacific monitored Japanese resource acquisition and strategic agricultural initiatives.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' index sheet for decimal file 894.61323, classified under Agriculture (Field Crops, Seeds, Fibers: Flax in Japan). It records a solitary entry: Despatch No. 1 from American Consul Calvin M. Hitch in Wellington, New Zealand, dated February 2, 1934, reporting on New Zealand press accounts concerning an order placed by Japan for forty thousand flax plants, with subsequent developments cross-referenced to file 847h.00/25.

subfiles.about: A Department of State list of papers recording a 1934 consular despatch from Wellington concerning a Japanese order of forty thousand flax plants from New Zealand.
subfiles.summary: This index sheet inventories documents filed under decimal classification 894.61323 relating to flax in Japan. It catalogues Despatch No. 1 dated February 2, 1934, from Consul Hitch in Wellington, New Zealand, which reported local press coverage regarding a substantial Japanese order for forty thousand flax plants. The entry notes that further developments regarding this matter were recorded under cross-reference 847h.00/25.
